candidates.reason: For issue I1 about whether the contract validly incorporated promises about the fireworks, Carlill v Carbolic Smoke Ball Co (J23) is highly relevant as it shows how an advertisement and promises made can be incorporated as binding terms if there is clear intention to be bound and performance or deposit indicating acceptance. Adams v Lindsell (J27) and Hyde v Wrench (J26) clarify offer and acceptance principles including counter-offers. Olley v Marlborough Court Ltd (J42) and L'Estrange v F Graucob Ltd (J40) cover incorporation of terms and notice before contract formation. The hybrid shortlist cases Partridge v Crittenden (J24) and Fisher v Bell (J50) are classic authorities on offers and invitations to treat, useful against incorporation.

candidates.reason: For issue I2 on frustration by cancellation of the fireworks, Krell v Henry (J37) is the leading case where cancellation of a central event frustrated a contract for hire of a viewing flat, directly analogous here. Herne Bay Steam Boat Co v Hutton (J38) and Taylor v Caldwell (J36) speak to when frustration does and does not apply based on the foundation and impossibility doctrines. Davis Contractors Ltd v Fareham Urban District Council (J39) distinguishes hardship from frustrating events. Merritt v Merritt (J30) is relevant for contractual obligations and their discharge. Alcock v Chief Constable (J15) is less central but included for completeness on event-related claims. Fisher v Bell (J50) from the shortlist is less relevant here but noted.
